newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Hungary's Goncz arrives for Brazil trade visit.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Goncz arrives for Brazil trade visit.

text.p: Hungarian President Arpad Goncz arrived in Brazil on Wednesday at the start of a week-long visit aimed at improving economic ties, Brazilian Foreign Ministry officials said.
Goncz, accompanied by about 50 leading businessmen, was scheduled to preside over a Brazil-Hungarian business forum before heading to the capital Brasilia later in the day.

"The visit has a strong economic-commercial element. But it also has a political angle in that it allows us to exchange views and experiences," said Debora Baremboim, head of the Brazilian Foreign Ministry's East and Central Europe Department.
Goncz will meet President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in Brasilia on Thursday for talks expected to focus on trade and investment opportunities.
Bilateral trade was less than $200 million in 1996, with Brazil enjoying a rare trade surplus with Hungary.

Baremboim said businessmen accompanying Goncz would be looking at possible ventures in health, heavy machinery and transport. She said Hungary considered Brazil a gateway to the Mercosur trade bloc, which groups Brazil with Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.
Cardoso and Goncz are expected to sign accords on air travel, tourism and work permits for diplomats' spouses.

After a day of official engagements in Brasilia, Goncz will visit industrial powerhouse Sao Paulo. On Saturday, he travels to the Foz de Iguacu waterfalls on Brazil's southern border before heading by road on Sunday to Argentina. He is also scheduled to visit Chile.
